=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: lines 21176-21189 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The progress baseline fingerprint is captured before `ensure_security_pass_state_fields` normalizes fields that the fingerprint includes, so normalization alone can be recorded as project progress and queue a follow-up poll.
  WHY: The baseline and persisted-state fingerprints differ when security-pass fields are normalized; severity is MAJOR according to Minimax and NIT according to Sonnet, Luna, and Qwen.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: Line: 3048-3052 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The progress fingerprinting logic captures the state before normalization by `ensure_security_pass_state_fields`.
  WHY: Adding missing security-pass fields to reach a default state changes the fingerprint despite no real project movement, causing an unnecessary follow-up poll.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml: lines 1109-1165 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The “Queue a follow-up poll after progress” step lacks `continue-on-error: true`, so a non-zero helper exit can fail the poll job after its primary work has succeeded.
  WHY: The step runs after the poller has completed its work and persisted state; Sonnet disputes this failure path, reporting that the helper exits 0 on every path.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml: 1111-1120 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The follow-up step does not pass the `AI_MEMORY_ENABLED` repository variable to the helper.
  WHY: Repository variables are not automatically exported to step processes, so the helper defaults the unset variable to true and can read or write force-tick records despite the documented memory kill switch being false.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh: 334-418 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The 300-second cooldown is fail-open when the memory ledger cannot be read or claimed, allowing dispatch without a persisted cooldown claim.
  WHY: With a flapping project state, progressing ticks can queue follow-up runs without the cooldown; severity is MAJOR according to Gemini, Minimax, Luna, and Qwen, and NIT according to Sonnet, which says this is existing documented behavior and not a defect in the diff.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml: 1110-1165 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The follow-up relies on a fail-open memory-ledger cooldown claim to enforce its 300-second interval.
  WHY: If the force-tick memory claim or its re-read fails, the helper proceeds with dispatch, so a subsequent progressing tick can dispatch again inside the cooldown window.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml: the new step "Queue a follow-up poll after progress" (about line 1113 onward) | severity=low | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: Each progress-triggered follow-up is a full poller tick against the shared `GH_PAT` quota, and this step adds no rate-limit circuit-breaker gate.
  WHY: Under rate-limit pressure, progress-triggered follow-ups can run up to once per 300 seconds per project; Sonnet describes this as design context and does not request a change.
- README.md: line 1444 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The README still describes polling as driven entirely by the wrapper cron and says the end-of-run self-retrigger was removed, despite the new conditional follow-up dispatch.
  WHY: Operators investigating extra poll runs are told that no such dispatch exists.
- README.md: Line: 198 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The README description still suggests that polling is driven entirely by the wrapper cron and that self-triggering is removed.
  WHY: Operators may not know to check the new step, its kill switch, or its cooldown when investigating extra poll runs.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml: lines 1113-1165 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The follow-up step executes a helper that performs a `workflow_dispatch` API call, but the step and its input description do not advertise that capability.
  WHY: With the feature enabled by default and memory unavailable, progressing ticks can repeatedly trigger self-dispatches and consume shared PAT quota; the workflow input description does not declare the kill switch.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: lines 21177-21179 (baseline capture) followed by the call to `ensure_security_pass_state_fields` (defined at line 5777) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: `POLL_PROGRESS_BASELINE_FP` is computed from the loaded state before `ensure_security_pass_state_fields` runs, even though that function rewrites two fingerprinted fields.
  WHY: If the normalized state is persisted through `post_state_comment`, the fingerprint differs from the baseline and the first tick on a legacy or partial state counts normalization as project progress, queuing one extra tick.
- scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh: lines 340-342 and 400-417 (memory read, claim and re-read failures all continue to dispatch) | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The 300 s cooldown is enforced only through the ai-memory ledger, and the helper dispatches without a persisted claim if the ledger cannot be read or claimed.
  WHY: A ledger outage plus a flapping fingerprinted field can queue a follow-up every tick; this is existing documented fail-open behavior shared by other callers, not a defect in this diff.
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml: the new step "Queue a follow-up poll after progress" (about line 1113 onward) | severity=low | confidence=[1]
  PROBLEM: Each follow-up is a full poller tick against the shared `GH_PAT` quota, and this step adds no rate-limit circuit-breaker gate.
  WHY: Under rate-limit pressure, progress-triggered follow-ups keep running at up to one per 300 s per project, the same worst case as the intended `*/5` cadence; no change is requested.
- README.md: line 1444 (the `orchestrate_poll.yml` row) and line 2881 (step 5, "Polling") | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Both lines still say polling is driven entirely by the wrapper cron and that the end-of-run `workflow_dispatch` self-retrigger was removed.
  WHY: An operator investigating an extra poll run is told no such dispatch exists.

=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
